1: The Moon is 384,000 km from Earth.
2: People first stepped on the Moon on July 20, 1969 (Apollo 11).
3: The Moon is about a quarter as wide as Earth.
4: The Moon is silent: there's no air, so astronauts talk by radio.
5: The solar wind rushes out at about 400 km per second.
6: About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
7: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 °C hot.
8: The Sun holds 99.8% of the Solar System's mass.
9: The Sun is 4.5 billion years old — about halfway through its life.
10: The SOHO observatory has watched the Sun since 1995.
11: In the daytime the Moon heats up to 127 °C — hotter than boiling water.
12: The Moon's "seas" are frozen lava, not water.
13: With no wind or rain, Moon craters last billions of years.
14: The Moon doesn't glow — it reflects sunlight.
15: The Apollo 8 crew took the "Earthrise" photo in 1968.
17: Parker Solar Probe is the fastest machine people have ever built.
18: 12 astronauts have walked on the Moon.
19: Apollo brought 382 kg of Moon rocks back to Earth.
20: Moon dust is sharp and sticky, like tiny bits of glass.
21: On the Moon you can jump 6 times higher!
22: The Moon drifts 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
23: The Moon's pull makes the ocean tides.
24: Green auroras come from oxygen, purple ones from nitrogen.
25: There is ice in dark craters near the Moon's pole.
26: The Moon probably formed when a Mars-sized body hit Earth.
27: Light from the nearest star after the Sun takes over 4 years to reach us.
28: NASA forecasters watch the Sun to keep astronauts safe.
29: Artemis will land people on the Moon again, near its south pole.
30: Apollo footprints are still on the Moon: there's no wind.
